questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good academic school and preferably in London

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite challenging. I definitely feel that both KU and King's College are lacking proper and clear communication with their exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many emails from the exchange-office at King's College and an introductory Zoom-meeting. And 1 hour "tea and greatings" with the other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They did nearly nothing to make it easier for us to meet other exchange students (or other students in general). One thing is simple orientation about the school and the general practical aspects of it. But another extremely important part of an exchange programme is the social aspect; meeting other students. And this was so disappointing. I attended one musical, where other exchange students were invited. And then I atteneded a 1 hour event where King's College just booked a room and then placed some cookies and tea. There was no host, no introduction - just 100 exchange students in one tiny room for an hour, trying to "network". And after this, there was nothing else. During my time, I made nearly no new friends (and I am extremely social), because we haden't gotten a proper introduction to anyone. I almost didn't see any exchange students (maybe except for a few Danes, that I knew beforehand).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult! I lived at a Danish hostel for three weeks (KFUK) and in this time I was trying to find an apartement for short let (only 3 months). Luckily I was with my friend from KU, but we went through a lot of bad viewings and annoying real estate agents.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do not try to rent your own apartement! It is not easy and the standards in London are horrible. Choose King's College accomodation or AirBnb - even though it seems expensive. You will (most likely) not find anything cheaper and it is not worth the hassle!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't know that exchange students were aloud accomodation - or it at least seemed like it was really difficult.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get an email and then you follow the instructions. After being admitted, I had to pick 10 different courses we wanted to attend and then after (quite) a while I was placed in four courses. They were not all my first pick, but luckily I did get the two that were mandatory at KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always write to King's College exchange-office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got my two favorite and the other two were a but more random.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be frustrating but do your best and just send King's College an email if you have any question. I will be worth it in the end <3

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I loved the courses! Academically King's College is great - or especially the classes I took. All great teachers/professors, who were very passionate about what they were teaching.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different but great to try! We were often only between 7-15 in a classroom and participation was greatly encouraged. I am not normally fond of speaking in class, but this pushed me (in a comfortable way) and it made me gain a deeper insight in the litterature.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I attended: Authoritarianism, Global Power Europe, Comparative European Politics and Contemporary German Politics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend: 
- Authoritarianism: The professor is so knowledgeable and it was great to learn about other regimes than democratic
- Global Power Europe: Tomas is amazing! I have never learned this much in such a short time. And he makes topics in the EU interesting :)
- Comparative European Politics: This is much more basic and based on litterature that we have learned in DAK. However, it was nice to use my existing knowledge in the classroom, where debates were encouraged. This was not a very challenging course, but it was nice to feel much "at home" in a subject.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I attended the Running Club a few times - that was great

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Watch musicals!
Eat as much Indian food as possible!
Fun destinations
- Seven Sisters (small hike, 2 hour train ride from London)
- Bath (Roman Baths, 2 hour train ride from London)
- Cardiff (Cute at Christmas, 2 hour train ride from London)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - England is very much like Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The quality of housing - the standard is horrible.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I loved the English people - they are so kind and welcoming!
I loved London as a city - there is always something to do and something to eat!
I loved that they took their academic career seriously - it really rubbed off on me!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Choose accomodation
- Be prepared to use quite a bit of money - but enjoy it and save up before!
- Try to really engage in the courses and read the literature, it will make your experience much better at King's.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow KFUK on instagram and perhaps try to see if they have available rooms or maybe just start by living there for a few weeks. You get to meet many Danish students and it is a great way to start.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Learning so much more about the EU!
Being independent in one of the biggest cities in Europe!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Please enjoy - it is amazing despite all the obstacles!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
